statements.statement: A single transistor on its own can add numbers and store information.
statements.explanation: A single transistor can only say ON or OFF. It takes billions of transistors wired together to create circuits that can add numbers, compare values, and store information.

statements.statement: Modern computer chips contain billions of transistors, each smaller than a virus.
statements.explanation: Transistors have been shrunk to an incredibly small scale. A modern chip packs billions of them together, and each one is smaller than a biological virus.

statements.statement: Computers need billions of transistors because each individual transistor is very slow.
statements.explanation: The reason is not speed but capability. A single transistor can only switch ON or OFF. Useful work like adding numbers or running games requires combining enormous numbers of these simple switches into complex circuits.
